excerpt: A 13x11 cedar greenhouse with a pergola entrance, 143 sq ft of floor, 48 linear feet of staging and a 9,200 lb snow rating.
description:
The Bellerose XL is the large-format version of the same idea: a pergola and trellis roof over the entrance for climbing vines, and a serious amount of room behind it. There are 143 square feet of floor and 48 linear feet of staging across upper and lower shelves, enough to run seed trays, potting and mature plants at once without moving things aside.
Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, retaining roughly 30% more heat than the 6mm twin-wall found on most greenhouses, and diffusing direct sun into even light. Four casement windows and a thermostat-activated exhaust fan handle a structure this size, where still air builds up faster than in a small frame.
The frame is FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar, which resists rot and insects without treatment. An interior spigot and collapsible hose are included, and the structure is tested to 9,200 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.
highlights: 143 sq ft interior with 48 linear feet of upper and lower staging shelves
Integrated pergola with trellis roof over the entrance
10mm four-wall polycarbonate, R-2.1 — about 30% more heat retention than 6mm twin-wall
FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar frame, naturally rot and insect resistant
Thermostat-activated exhaust fan plus four casement windows
Interior water spigot with collapsible hose included
Tested to 9,200 lb snow load and 100 mph winds
Room to run seed trays, potting and mature plants at the same time

excerpt: A 14.5x12 cedar greenhouse with a chalet-style gabled roof, 161 sq ft inside and a built-in stainless steel sink.
description:
A steep gabled roofline and exposed framing give the Savannah a chalet silhouette rather than the usual garden-shed profile. It is the largest cedar frame in the range at 161 square feet, with 55 linear feet of staging across upper and lower shelves.
The detail that separates it is a built-in stainless steel sink with water connections, so cleaning pots and cutting stems happens in the greenhouse instead of at the outside tap. An interior spigot with collapsible hose is included as well.
Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, holding around 30% more heat than 6mm twin-wall and diffusing light so nothing scorches. Two thermostat-activated exhaust fans and four casement windows move air through a footprint this size. The frame is FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar, and the structure is tested to 9,950 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.

Built-in stainless steel sink with water connections
Steep gabled roofline with exposed framing, chalet-inspired

excerpt: A 14x12 metal-framed greenhouse with 163 sq ft inside, 500 lb shelves, gutters and a 10,600 lb snow rating.
description:
The Larkspur is the one built from metal rather than cedar. A black galvanised steel and aluminium frame sits on oversized 4.7-inch corner posts, with wood-tone composite panelling that gives the warmth of timber without the maintenance that comes with it.
Inside there are 163 square feet and 44 linear feet of staging rated to 500 lb per shelf, which matters if you are standing heavy planters or bagged compost on them rather than seed trays. Two thermostat-activated exhaust fans and four windows with removable magnetic screens handle airflow, and the screens mean the windows can stay open without letting insects in.
Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, about 30% better at holding heat than 6mm twin-wall. Residential-grade aluminium gutters route roof water away from the base rather than letting it pool. An interior spigot and exterior inlet are included, and the structure is tested to 10,600 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds — the highest rating in the range.

Galvanised steel and aluminium frame on oversized 4.7" corner posts
Wood-tone composite panelling — timber look without the maintenance
Two thermostat-activated exhaust fans plus four windows with magnetic insect screens

Residential-grade aluminium gutters route roof water clear of the base

excerpt: A 9x6 cedar greenhouse with a pergola entrance, 54 sq ft of floor and 19 linear feet of staging shelves.
description:
The 9x6 Bellerose is the compact version of the pergola-fronted design, sized for a garden where a 13-foot frame would dominate. The trellis roof over the entrance still gives climbing vines and hanging baskets somewhere to go, so the greenhouse reads as part of the planting rather than a box dropped beside it.
Inside there are 54 square feet with 19 linear feet of upper and lower staging. Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, retaining about 30% more heat than the 6mm twin-wall most greenhouses use, and diffusing sun into even light instead of hot spots.
A thermostat-activated exhaust fan and one casement window cover airflow at this size. The frame is FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar, resisting rot and insects without chemical treatment, and an interior water spigot is included. Tested to 3,700 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.

excerpt: The 9x6 Bellerose in a pre-stained white finish — pergola entrance, 54 sq ft of floor, 19 linear feet of staging.
description:
The same 9x6 pergola-fronted Bellerose, finished in white. The cedar is pre-stained and sealed at the factory, so the colour is on the timber before it arrives and there is no painting to do on assembly — which also means the finish reaches the joints and end grain that are awkward to coat once a frame is standing.
Inside there are 54 square feet with 19 linear feet of upper and lower staging, and the trellis roof over the entrance carries climbing vines and hanging baskets. Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, holding roughly 30% more heat than 6mm twin-wall while diffusing direct sun.
Airflow runs on a thermostat-activated exhaust fan with one casement window. The cedar still resists rot, decay and insects under the finish, an interior water spigot is included, and the structure is tested to 3,700 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.

excerpt: A 9x6 cedar greenhouse with a three-sided trellis roof, 50 sq ft inside and 26 linear feet of staging with a 4-tier rack.
description:
The 9x6 Poppy keeps the three-sided trellis roof of its larger sibling, which is the point of the design: the outside of the frame carries hanging baskets and climbing vines, so a small greenhouse grows more than its floor area suggests.
Inside there are 50 square feet with 26 linear feet of staging across upper and lower shelves, including a four-tier rack that stacks pots vertically instead of spreading them along a bench. In a frame this size that is the difference between working room and shuffling things around.
Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, retaining about 30% more heat than 6mm twin-wall and turning direct sun into diffused light. A thermostat-activated exhaust fan and one casement window handle airflow. The frame is FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar, an interior spigot with collapsible hose is included, and the structure is tested to 2,600 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.

excerpt: A 9x6 cedar greenhouse with a contemporary sloped roof, 54 sq ft of floor and 13 linear feet of lower staging.
description:
The Willow is the plainest frame in the range, and deliberately so. A contemporary sloped roof and clean lines give it a compact, minimal profile that sits alongside a modern house without looking like a garden outbuilding.
Inside there are 54 square feet with 13 linear feet of lower staging. The shelving sits low rather than running upper and lower, which leaves the upper volume clear — useful if what you are growing goes up rather than out.
Glazing is 10mm four-wall polycarbonate rated R-2.1, holding around 30% more heat than the 6mm twin-wall used on most greenhouses this size, and diffusing sun so plants get even coverage. A thermostat-activated exhaust fan and one casement window handle airflow. The frame is FSC-certified kiln-dried cedar, which resists rot and insects untreated, an interior water spigot is included, and the structure is tested to 2,800 lb of snow load and 100 mph winds.
